chunks: He (peace be upon him) said to a man who had requested him to preach:

O man, indeed Allah, the Exalted, did not create you in vain, nor leave you idle, but He created you to test you and examine you; so whoever is patient succeeds, and whoever is grateful is given more.
ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of human creation according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this discourse from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the teleological purpose of human existence, framing life as a divine test (ibtila') rather than a state of idleness. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on active spiritual engagement, where patience (sabr) and gratitude (shukr) serve as the twin pillars for achieving success and divine favor.
